references.text: Jesus' reputation spread throughout all of Syria, and great crowds followed him to be healed—a parallel to how the report about Jesus spread in Luke 5:15, where people came to hear and be healed.
The report about Jesus spread throughout the whole region after a healing, corresponding to the spreading of the word about him in Luke 5:15.
The news about Jesus immediately spread throughout all of Galilee, thematically paralleling the spread of the report in Luke 5:15.
After the healing of the leper, the man began to tell about it, so that Jesus could no longer enter a town openly. This is Mark's version of the same event underlying Luke 5:15.
Great crowds from many places came to Jesus because they had heard all he was doing—paralleling the crowds that flocked together in Luke 5:15.
The report about Jesus spread throughout the whole region, and he was praised by everyone. This forms the background for the growing fame described further in Luke 5:15.
The news about Jesus went out to all places in the surrounding area, an earlier reference in Luke to the same phenomenon of spreading reports.
A large crowd came to hear him and be healed of their diseases—nearly identical wording to Luke 5:15 regarding coming to hear and be healed.
Thousands of people gathered around Jesus, expressing the enormous influx that began already in Luke 5:15.
A great crowd followed Jesus because they saw the signs he performed on the sick—a parallel motif with the crowds who came for healing in Luke 5:15.
